anomalies.observed: C4 is specified with value "100n" and a 1206 capacitor footprint, while C1, C2, and C3 are all 100u with the same LCSC part (C15008).
anomalies.expected: C4 should be 100uF to match the specification's servo power rail bulk capacitance: C1–C4 are all 100 µF × 4.

evidence.quote: C1–C4 | 100 µF × 4 | Bulk capacitance on the servo power rail (downstream of D2), buffering the high inrush current of PWM servos.

anomalies.impact: The servo power rail has only 300.1 µF of bulk capacitance instead of 400 µF, reducing its ability to buffer PWM servo inrush current and potentially causing the M5Stack to brown out or power down during servo movement.

parsed.summary: The design files contain one clear anomaly: C4 on the servo power rail is specified as 100n instead of the intended 100uF, reducing the bulk capacitance required for PWM servo inrush buffering.

R1 between +3V3 and TXD2 is a pull-up on TXD2, ensuring that if the UART pin is high-impedance, TXD2 is pulled high, keeping Q2 off. That is a common addition.
